name: Goa
title: Holidays in Goa
intro: Palm-fringed beaches, Portuguese churches and one of India's biggest Christmas celebrations. Here's what Goa is like with the family, when to go and how long to stay.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 4½ to 5½ hrs ahead of the UK

facts_note: Most visitors need an Indian e-Visa, applied for online before you go. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: November to March is dry and sunny, and Christmas is the liveliest and busiest time, with midnight mass, stars hung outside houses and parties on the beach. April and May get very hot, and the monsoon runs June to September.

things.name: South Goa beaches
things.blurb: Benaulim, Varca and Palolem are calmer and quieter than the north, with soft sand and gentle waves.

things.name: Christmas in Goa
things.blurb: Goa has a big Catholic community, so churches fill for midnight mass and villages light up with paper stars and cribs.

things.name: Old Goa
things.blurb: Grand Portuguese churches, including the Basilica of Bom Jesus, a World Heritage Site.

things.name: Fontainhas
things.blurb: The old Latin quarter of Panaji, with brightly painted houses and narrow lanes.

things.name: Spice plantation
things.blurb: A walk through a spice farm with a buffet lunch on banana leaves.

things.name: Dolphin spotting
things.blurb: Early morning boat trips go looking for dolphins off the coast.

faqs.question: Is Goa good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's good value, warm in winter and relaxed, especially in South Goa.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: Yes, British passport holders need an Indian e-Visa, applied for online before you travel. Check GOV.UK for the current rules.

faqs.question: North or South Goa?
faqs.answer: North Goa is livelier, with markets and nightlife. South Goa has quieter, cleaner beaches and suits families better.

faqs.question: Is Christmas a good time to go?
faqs.answer: Yes, the weather is perfect and the festivities are lovely, but prices peak, so book well ahead.
